CORRECTION_retraction.corrected_finding: Along the CLEAN-CLOSE trajectory (flat-scene capture), the full finger assembly CLEARS the 2-slot scene in X, Y, and Z with 4-10mm margin everywhere. The 29mm slots were NOT the obstruction. The video-observed 30-45deg finger tilt/splay is therefore NOT a geometric strike along the intended path -- it is a CONTACT-DYNAMICS divergence: in the supported scene the compliant 4-bar fingers deviate from the clean close (flop/splay). Whether a flopped finger then grazes a slot edge is a downstream consequence, not the initiating cause.
CORRECTION_retraction.why_this_matters: The (b) re-run as specified (widen slots per leg-F re-dimensioning, then rerun) would NOT fix the confound -- the slots already fit. This is the (a) gate working: it caught a wrong design direction (slot widening) before spending GPU on a re-run that could not have resolved the bend-rescue question. The gate verdict is NOT '(b)-feasible' -- it is 'the premise for (b) is refuted'.
CORRECTION_retraction.most_likely_actual_mechanism_UNRESOLVED: The central support that removes the cable sag ALSO makes the cable UNYIELDING (rests on solid at 0.804, cannot be pushed down). The flat-scene koshape grasp RELIES on the closing fingers pushing the cable DOWN ~6mm and hooking it from below (f1ext scoop); an unyielding cable may disrupt that scoop-and-cage, flopping the compliant 4-bar. This is a HYPOTHESIS (design-level, ties to Rs #3 'finger too high, dropping the cable'): central support may be geometrically fine yet mechanically incompatible with the scoop-cage grasp. NOT confirmable from static geometry or the flat capture -- needs an INSTRUMENTED re-run (persist per-frame claw z + finger/follower pose + cable z + contact) to observe the finger contact behavior directly.
CORRECTION_retraction.leg_F_verdict_supersede: the earlier gate_b_feasibility='FEASIBLE' answered the WRONG question (can 30mm slots + support coexist with DR20). Superseded: slots need no widening; the confound is not slot-width. Central-support geometry itself remains buildable (59mm nominal / 21mm at DR20).
CORRECTION_retraction.leg_Z2_A_verdict_supersede: (B) drive-asymmetry EXCLUSION STANDS (kinematic scene-independent drive, commanded dz 0.01mm, achieved <=0.037mm). But (A) 'edge-ride-up on UNDERSIZED slot' is REFUTED (slots not undersized). The observed per-arm claw asymmetry is therefore NEITHER drive NOR slot-narrowness -> it is compliant-finger CONTACT DYNAMICS (possibly per-arm asymmetric via 4-bar bistability) in the supported scene, OR partial video over-read. Resolvable only by the instrumented re-run.
CORRECTION_retraction.revised_recommendation_rule24: Do NOT launch the (b) re-run as 'widen slots + rerun' (premise refuted). Options for Rs: (1) INSTRUMENTED diagnostic re-run of the 2-slot scene (persist finger pose + cable z + contact) to characterize the contact divergence -- answers WHY the fingers flop under support; (2) reconsider whether central support is compatible with the scoop-cage grasp at all (the sag-removal benefit vs the scoop-disruption cost) -- this may reframe the whole slot concept; (3) the Rs #3 height insight (deeper park so the pinch meets the unyielding cable) can be tested CHEAPLY on the FLAT scene first (dz sweep, no slot rebuild) to isolate the height axis from the support axis.
